reviewer_reason: The test reproduces (exit 1, about 22 s) and the code facts hold. A5 says "No party can make it stop accepting them". But section 7's adversary list and section 4's untrusted column never give anyone guardian powers. The deployment picks the guardian, and GUARDIAN=0 turns foreclosure off. reviewer_severity: Out of scope (the guardian is a trusted emergency role that the deployment configures; preferred) / Critical (if A5's "No party" covers the guardian)
gap: The threat model never says whether governance roles that the deployment configures in the referee contracts are trusted parts of the deployment or "parties" under A5's "No party can make it stop accepting them". These roles are the guardian, with foreclose() (Application.sol), the owner (which DaveAppFactory renounces) and sentries. Section 2's definition of a deployment does not mention them, and neither do the adversary list in section 7 or the trust boundaries in section 4. The manual's referee model has no guardian at all. Two facts would decide it: whether the maintainers count guardian-held keys as trusted like the operator's host, and whether A5's "Conversely" clause was meant to rule out an emergency foreclosure that the deployment opted into (GUARDIAN can be address(0)).

reviewer_reason: The test exits 1 every time, but the expansion is the documented result (cm.h: "a JSON array of 2^log2... hashes"). §8: "A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect." The guest cannot raise the worst case, so the OOS clause "Average-case performance that does not change the worst-case cost" applies.
